mine: sat at the entrance of Enaim
note: Hebrew petah 'enayim is most likely a place name ("the opening of Enaim", cf. Enam in Josh 15:34); the KJV takes it as a common noun phrase ("opening of the eyes", i.e. a conspicuous spot).
Hebrew petil is a cord or string, here the cord on which the cylinder seal hung; "bracelets" is a guess. Also in v. 25.

kjv: the harlot, that [was] openly by the way side
mine: the shrine prostitute who was at Enaim by the road
note: Hirah uses qedeshah ("consecrated woman", a cult prostitute) rather than zonah (v. 15), a more respectable term; the KJV renders both as "harlot". "Openly" again takes ba'enayim as a common noun rather than the place Enaim.
